correctness.rationale: Signed overlap integration yields A=(sin(pi*nu*(2-tau))-2sin(pi*nu*tau))/(pi*nu) for 0<tau<1 and the single-sinc formula for 1<=tau<2. With r=(2-tau)/tau and T=pi*tau*nu, multiple nonzero Doppler zeros obey sin(rT)=2sinT and r cos(rT)=2cosT. Their squared identity excludes r<2; for r>2 it forces sinT and cosT nonzero, so F_TT=-2(r*r-1)sinT nonzero (exact doubles). At r=2 the exact factor 2sinT(cosT-1) gives simple odd-pi and cubic even-pi roots; division by nu changes only nu=0 into a quadratic zero. F_r=Tcos(rT) and F_TT are nonzero at double roots, giving fold curvature and a locally discrete solution set. Irrational torus recurrence and the displayed nonsingular Jacobian yield double-root parameters converging to every irrational r>2; hence countable dense delays below 2/3. All joint nodal zeros have nonvanishing full gradient. Three nondegenerate sample folds and direct overlap integrals were checked from the packaged checker, but finite checks do not prove the theorem.

value.rationale: The natural invariant is the failure of simple Doppler nulls as delay varies in the canonical signed rectangular (Haar) waveform. Countable density of double-zero delays, an exact global simplicity threshold, infinitely many cubic resonances at the endpoint, and the simultaneous nonsingularity of the full joint nodal manifold describe a qualitative caustic mechanism beyond routine evaluation of the elementary transform. The theorem distinguishes unbounded-frequency instability from finite-band zeros and has direct structural relevance to narrowband delay-Doppler resolution; no engineering performance guarantee is inferred.
